text:
elaine: Heads-up — customer hit a weird runtime failure only after bundling an SDK sample app for edge. Works in Node, fails in Vite->Cloudflare and webpack edge builds. Minimal repro below.

noah: paste error + package version?

elaine: using `redwood-inference-js@0.13.0`. Runtime error in worker: 
```
TypeError: createClient is not a function
  at fetch (/assets/entry.js:12:56)
```
Bundle analysis shows SDK was transformed into an ESM chunk that still contains a CommonJS wrapper and a `module.exports`->`exports.default` pattern, but the worker runtime ends up loading the wrong export.

connie: Interesting — different from the usual `exports is not defined` because here the default export was lost. Which bundlers reproduce?

elaine: Vite 4 + @cloudflare/wrangler, webpack 5 with worker-loader, and a Rollup-based edge adapter all reproduce. I reproduced with a tiny TS sample app (1 file) that imports `createClient` and calls `client.generate()`.

noah: Two quick workarounds that helped in different projects: 1) Vite: set `optimizeDeps.include` and `ssr.noExternal` to force ESM build of the package; 2) Webpack: add `resolve.alias` to point `redwood-inference-js` to the ESM file in the dist folder (e.g., `dist/index.mjs`) so it doesn't pick up the CJS bundle. Both are hacks.

connie: I also saw a TS typing problem — when bundlers externalize the package, TypeScript couldn't pick up the shipped .d.ts and users got `any` for client methods. Adding a top-level `types` field in package.json resolves that.

elaine: Repro steps I used:
1) `npm init -y && npm i vite@4 redwood-inference-js@0.13.0 @cloudflare/wrangler`
2) src/worker.ts:
```ts
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference-js';
export default {
  fetch() {
    const c = createClient({ apiKey: '__KEY' });
    return new Response('ok');
  }
}
```
3) `vite build --ssr` + publish to modules worker -> runtime crash.

noah: Packaging notes for SDK team: publish a pure ESM module without CommonJS interop helpers, add explicit `exports` with `import` and `require` targets, ensure `types` points at `dist/index.d.ts`, and include `module`/`main` fields consistently. Also set `sideEffects: false` to help bundlers tree-shake.

connie: Proposed CI check: build the tiny sample with Vite, Rollup, and Webpack and assert that the ESM assets don’t contain `module.exports` or `exports.` strings and that `createClient` is exported as a proper ESM named export. I can add a small test job to catch regressions.

build-bot: CI: sample-app-edge-typed build #981 failed earlier. Logs: https://ci.internal/981/logs (contains failing bundle diff).

elaine: I'll open an internal repro PR (single-file sample + minimal configs) and link the failing bundle. Will also attach the quick Vite/webpack workarounds in the DX doc so customers have something until packaging fix lands.

noah: thanks. filing SDK issue and tagging packaging + releases. PR link will go into the issue.
